issue.title: fix(suspense): keep the boundary pending while its branch is patched
issue.body:
Fix #7506
Related #8206, #8265, #15333

nuxt/nuxt#36249 is using the patch from part of this PR for a POC to fix issues caused when users navigate during hydration.

## Issue

When `patchSuspense` patches a pending branch with the same root type, a nested `<Suspense suspensible>` may resolve the parent before `patch()` finishes.

1. **Double resolve.** `patchSuspense` continues with stale `isInFallback` and `activeBranch` state, causing a second resolve or patching an already unmounted branch.

2. **Non-atomic patch.** Async components mounted later in the same patch cannot register dependencies after `pendingBranch` is cleared, causing fallback and `onResolve` to happen too early.

## Changes

Hold a sentinel dependency during the patch to keep the boundary pending until the patch finishes, then resolve based on the final `deps` count.

issue.body:
Fixes #5535

## Summary

- Change `injectLocal` from a `const` arrow export to a `function` declaration so Rollup/Rolldown can interpret the JSDoc `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` tag during bundling
- Matches the pattern used by other annotated exports in `@vueuse/shared` (e.g. `useArrayFind`, `useToggle`)

## Problem

When building a Nuxt 4 app for production, Nitro/Rollup emits a warning like:

```
A comment
"/**
* ...
* @__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__
*/"
in ".nuxt/dist/server/server.mjs" contains an annotation that Rollup cannot interpret due to the position of the comment. The comment will be removed to avoid issues.
```

`injectLocal` is currently exported as:

```ts
/** @__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__ */
export const injectLocal: typeof inject = <T>(...args) => { ... }
```

Rollup only understands `#__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` / `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` on **function declarations**, not on `const` bindings. `provideLocal` is a plain `function` without this JSDoc tag and does not trigger the warning.

## Reproduction

Minimal repro (Nuxt 4.5.2 + @vueuse/nuxt 14.4.0, `useBreakpoints()` in `app.vue`):

- **GitHub:** https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-vueuse-injectlocal-warning-repro
- **StackBlitz:** https://stackblitz.com/github/s00d/nuxt-vueuse-injectlocal-warning-repro

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm build
```

The warning appears during the **Nitro server bundle** step (after Vite SSR), not during client build or `nuxt dev`.

Applying a local patch that changes `const injectLocal` → `function injectLocal` in `@vueuse/shared` removes the warning (see `patches/@vueuse__shared@14.4.0.patch` in the repro repo).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test:unit packages/shared/injectLocal/index.test.ts`

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

comment.body:
To be more clear in short:

Using function overloads (this PR):
- **Pro:** We can add `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` to the JSDoc for human readers.
- **Con:** We can't reuse Vue's `inject` type directly, so we'd need to manually keep it in sync with any future changes.

Using `typeof inject` (PR #5613):
- **Pro:** We can reuse Vue's `inject` type directly.
- **Con:** We can't use `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` in the JSDoc, as it would be recognized by Rolldown and trigger a warning. However, we can use something similar for human readers, e.g. `@NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`, to avoid this.

Both of these 2 approaches can preserve the tree-shaking annotation functionality without triggering a Rolldown warning.

issue.title: fix: renderInlineAsync no longer routes async render through patched sync renderInline (#35)
issue.body:
## What

`Renderer.renderInlineAsync()` (new in `1.2.0`) delegated to a monkey-patched **sync** `renderInline` whenever one was present. When a plugin wraps *both* `renderInline` and `renderInlineAsync` — a natural, async-aware pattern (e.g. [`@comark/markdown-it`](https://github.com/comarkdown/comark)) — the async render was routed back through the sync path, which throws `Renderer.renderInline: async rule detected` in the presence of async inline rules (Shiki, KaTeX, etc.).

This scopes the sync fallback so it is honored **only when `renderInlineAsync` itself is not patched**. If a plugin also wraps `renderInlineAsync`, its async-aware wrapper has already run its preprocessing by the time control reaches the prototype method, so delegating to the sync path is both unnecessary and unsafe — instead the proper async loop runs.

The existing behavior of honoring a plugin that patches *only* `renderInline` is preserved.

Fixes #35.

## Why

This breaks real-world downstreams: Slidev decks with `comark: true` apply `@comark/markdown-it` on top of async Shiki/KaTeX inline rules, so `slidev build` fails on any install resolving `markdown-exit@1.2.0` (slidevjs/slidev#2717 pinned to `1.1.0-beta.2` as a stopgap).

## Verification

Added a TDD regression test that wraps both inline render methods with an async `code_inline` rule (the reproduction from the issue) — it fails before the fix with the reported error and passes after. Full suite (966 tests), lint, build, and typecheck all pass.

This PR was created with the help of an agent.

issue.title: renderInlineAsync() falls back to sync renderInline, throwing "async rule detected" when a plugin wraps the renderer
issue.body: ## Summary `renderInlineAsync()` (new in `1.2.0`) delegates to a monkey-patched **sync** `renderer.renderInline` whenever one is present, even when async inline rules are registered. Any plugin that wraps *both* `renderInline` and `renderInlineAsync` (a natural pattern) therefore routes the async render back through the sync path, which throws: ``` Error: Renderer.renderInline: async rule detected, use renderInlineAsync() ``` This looks like the `renderInline` counterpart of the "honor monkey-patched renderer" fallback added for #33 — but unlike `render`/`renderAsync`, the inline variant is unsafe. ## Root cause `Renderer.prototype.renderInlineAsync` (`dist/index.js`, ~L3697): ```js async renderInlineAsync(tokens, options, env) { const renderInline = this.renderInline if (renderInline !== Renderer.prototype.renderInline) return renderInline.call(this, tokens, options, env) // <-- sync fallback // ...proper async loop (Promise.all over rules)... } ``` When a plugin wraps `renderInline`, `this.renderInline !== Renderer.prototype.renderInline`, so `renderInlineAsync` calls the **sync** `renderInline`. If an inline rule is async (Shiki, KaTeX, etc.), the sync `renderInline` hits its own `isPromiseLike` guard and throws. Crucially, a plugin that is async-aware and *also* wraps `renderInlineAsync` has already run its preprocessing in its own async wrapper by the time control reaches the prototype method — so delegating to the sync path is both unnecessary and wrong. ## Minimal reproduction (markdown-exit only) ```js import MarkdownExit from 'markdown-exit' const md = new MarkdownExit({ html: true }) // A plugin that wraps BOTH renderInline and renderInlineAsync, only // preprocessing tokens then delegating (the @comark/markdown-it pattern). const wrap = fn => function (tokens, options, env) { // real plugins mutate `tokens` here return fn.call(this, tokens, options, env) } md.renderer.renderInline = wrap(md.renderer.renderInline) md.renderer.renderInlineAsync = wrap(md.renderer.renderInlineAsync) // An async inline rule, as Shiki/KaTeX register in real apps md.renderer.rules.code_inline = async (tokens, i) => { await Promise.resolve() return `${tokens[i].content}` } await md.renderAsync('a `b` c\n') // THROWS: Renderer.renderInline: async rule detected, use renderInlineAsync() ``` - `1.1.0-beta.2`: renders fine (no such fallback). - `1.2.0`: throws. ## Real-world impact This breaks [Slidev](https://github.com/slidevjs/slidev): decks with `comark: true` apply [`@comark/markdown-it`](https://github.com/comarkdown/comark) (which wraps both inline render methods) on top of async Shiki/KaTeX inline rules, so `slidev build` fails on every fresh install that resolves `markdown-exit` to `1.2.0`. We've pinned to `1.1.0-beta.2` as a stopgap (slidevjs/slidev#2717) and would love to unpin once this is fixed. ## Suggested fix `renderInlineAsync` should not blindly delegate to a patched **sync** `renderInline`. Options: - Run the async loop directly and drop the sync fallback for the inline path (a patched `renderInlineAsync`, which async-aware plugins wrap, is what gets called anyway); or - Only take the fallback when no async inline rule is present. I verified locally that replacing `renderInlineAsync` with a plain async loop (`Promise.all` over the rules, no sync fallback) renders the Slidev + comark + async-rule case correctly. ## Environment - markdown-exit: `1.2.0` (broken), `1.1.0-beta.2` (works) - @comark/markdown-it: `0.3.4` - Node: reproduced on current LTS _Filed with the help of an agent._

> Always use shallowRef() instead of ref() for primitive values (string, number, boolean, null, etc.) for better performance.

issue.title: Reactivity rules about shallowRef
issue.body:
Hello, regarding https://github.com/vuejs-ai/skills/blob/main/skills/vue-best-practices/references/reactivity.md and especially the rule about `shallowRef`

> Always use shallowRef() instead of ref() for primitive values (string, number, boolean, null, etc.) for better performance.

I wonder to what extent this is relevant regarding primitive values.

Vue official doc https://vuejs.org/api/reactivity-advanced.html#shallowref

> shallowRef() is typically used for performance optimizations of large data structures, or integration with external state management systems.

Thank you for clarification.

comment.body:
Thanks for the question. `shallowRef()` is essentially a `ref()` without deep reactivity. For primitive values, there is no deep reactivity involved in the first place, so `ref()` and `shallowRef()` behave the same from a reactivity perspective.

When `ref()` is used with a non-primitive value such as an object or array, Vue will convert the value to a deeply reactive proxy. `shallowRef()`, on the other hand, keeps the inner value as-is and only makes `.value` reactive.

The reasoning behind this rule when I wrote it was mainly that these best practices are intended for AI-generated code. Since the code is generated by AI, the idea was to favor the slightly more performance-oriented choice, even at the cost of being a bit less idiomatic.

That said, for primitive values specifically, this is only a micro-optimization. The rule is not meant to imply that using `ref()` with primitives causes significant deep-reactivity overhead.

issue.title: Define Style coding convention
issue.body:
As discussed in the meeting, we would like to have a rule of coding convention about writing styles.
Please help create a document about the practice of writing CSS style attached with the created PRs as an example for reference.
I think the below points need to be emphasized, please feel free to add it if there are other concerns.

- Writing inline style as first option, and write class alternatively if the style is not supported by tailwindcss.
- If there exists duplicated css style in the common HTML structure, please consider extracting it as another component with unified style definitions.
- The content in i18n should be limited to items that require translation. Unrelated content such as external links, icons should be avoided. PR#395 is an example of this.
- Comments should only be added to code that contains useful information for programming. Avoid adding comments to code that is uncertain or about to be deleted.
- The code files related to the schedule page are good examples that follow the above points.

issue.title: [Bug] 議程頁若有 Slido 會無法返回上一頁
issue.body:
## Description

在議程頁面與 keynote 頁停留幾秒，會使「回上一頁」功能異常，需要多次點擊才能回到上一頁。

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 在時間表頁面，點擊任一個議程
2. 確認進入 [keynote](https://tw.pycon.org/2024/zh-hant/conference/keynotes) 或 [talk](https://tw.pycon.org/2024/zh-hant/conference/talk/<id>) 頁
3. 確認有 Slido 的 tab，等幾秒再按上一頁。(等待過程不用做任何事
4. 無法回到時間表

## More Information

問題出在 Slido 的 iframe 會更改 window.history。
一個簡單的處理方法，是讓 iframe 在點開 Slido tab 時再出現就好。但是點開 Slido tab，還是會遇到問題。

issue.title: nuxt build halts the machine
issue.body:
The app is currently running on a GCE g1-small (0.5vCPU & 1.7GB memory). `docker-compose up -d --build` is used for deploying, but it started to occasionally halt the entire machine in the past month. Cannot be reproduced in the staging environment.

- We might need to make sure we did not create any change that leads to memory leakage first. 
- Should also check if it's an issue regarding docker settings.
- One of the possible reasons is the building process takes up a significant amount of memory but g1-small only has 1.7 Gb. Due to the limited budget, limiting the memory usage of the building process would be a better option than upgrading the machine type.

comment.body: The memory leak issue has been resolved by increasing the machine’s swap memory and the `max-old-space-size` Node.js option.

issue.title: fix(language-core): generate full fragment props for typecheck
issue.body:
Related #5769

This PR fixed expected type check for `<template>` props.

- Fixed: `__VLS_asFunctionalElement` is split since #5845
- New feature: Generate failed expressions for handling props like `@[x.bar]="x.baz()"`

comment.body:
I think it makes sense to keep this behavior from the language tools perspective, for a few reasons:

* Before #5769, `generateElement` would also check failed expressions.
* We still perform the same checks in other dead-code scenarios, for example after `v-if="false"`.
* If a user changes `<div v-for>` to `<template v-for>`, we probably shouldn’t suddenly silently ignore type errors.

Alternatively, another approach would be to emit an error or warning telling the user that these props will never be evaluated.
